title: The Yield Curve as a Predictor of U.S. Recessions
quote: significantly outperforms other financial and macroeconomic indicators in predicting recessions
note: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Current Issues in Economics and Finance, Vol. 2, No. 7, June 1996. Uses the 10-year minus 3-month spread.

title: The Yield Curve as a Leading Indicator: Frequently Asked Questions
quote: with a lead time of about four to six quarters
note: PDF opened and text extracted on 2026-11-09 (dated October 2005). The live recession-probability data sits behind an interactive page (ycfaq#/interactive) with no direct file link found, so the NY Fed benchmark series was NOT obtained.

title: Predicting Recession Probabilities Using the Slope of the Yield Curve
quote: may overstate the current probability of a recession
note: FEDS Notes, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 1 March 2018. Argues lower term premiums can make the raw slope overstate recession risk.

title: The cauldron has cooled down: a systematic literature review on home advantage in football during the COVID-19 pandemic from a socio-economic and psychological perspective
quote: the home advantage indeed decreases considerably during ghost games
note: Management Review Quarterly (online 4 Jan 2022). Also: leagues 'resumed in the form of ghost games in May and June 2020'; effect is 'league dependent'; mechanism mostly reduced referee bias.

title: No Fans-No Pressure: Referees in Professional Football During the COVID-19 Pandemic
quote: Since there were no significant changes in referee decisions against the away teams
note: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living 3:720488. 8 leagues, 1,286 matches (2018/19 vs 2019/20 ghost games), transfermarkt data. Disagrees with the review on the referee mechanism.
